chain.title: Sticks and Planks, Nothing Yet
chain.desc: Four sticks and four planks in a ring give four Framed Cubes. On its own it is a bare frame; right-click it with almost any full block and it takes on that block's texture, and every other item in the mod is cut from this one.

chain.title: The Tool That Reshapes
chain.desc: A framed cube and two sticks on a diagonal. The hammer is used as a crafting ingredient - it is not consumed - to cut a plain shape into its sharper relatives, and in the world it toggles waterlogging, prism offsets and item-frame backgrounds.

chain.title: Turning a Shape on Its Side
chain.desc: Two framed cubes over a stick handle. Every panel converts to its slab and every slab back to its panel by crafting it with the wrench, and in the world it sets a one-way window's see-through face and flips slope split-lines.

chain.title: The Small Adjustment
chain.desc: A wooden rod and one framed cube, diagonally. The third tool in the set and the cheapest, it exists for the state tweaks the hammer and wrench do not cover.

chain.title: Half a Frame
chain.desc: Three framed cubes in a row yield six slabs. This and the panel are the two halves the whole geometry library is built from, and the wrench turns each into the other for free.

chain.title: The Slab Stood Upright
chain.desc: Six per three cubes on the vertical. A panel is a slab rotated onto its edge, which is why so many later shapes come in matching panel and slab spellings.

chain.title: Steps in Disguise
chain.desc: Four stairs from six framed cubes. Add the wrench to convert them into Vertical Stairs, and the slope family below covers everything stairs cannot.

chain.title: The Diagonal
chain.desc: Three slopes from three cubes in an L. The slope is the root of the mod's largest family - prisms, corner slopes, slope panels and slope slabs all descend from this one block.

chain.title: A Post to Build Around
chain.desc: Shapeless from a Framed Corner Pillar. Pillars, half pillars and corner pillars are the vertical trim that the slope family has no answer for.

chain.title: Stop Crafting One at a Time
chain.desc: Three framed cubes under an iron ingot. The saw is a workbench that converts any framed block into any other of equal material value in one operation, and it is the point where the mod stops being a crafting grid exercise.

chain.title: The Saw That Runs Itself
chain.desc: Three framed cubes under an iron ingot flanked by redstone. The powered saw is the same conversion on Forge Energy, with a target slot you set by clicking it with any framed block.

chain.title: Copy the Whole Configuration
chain.desc: One sheet of paper ringed by four framed cubes. The blueprint records a framed block's shape, camo, illumination, intangibility and reinforcement together, and refuses only fluid camos.

chain.title: Sixteen Per Ring of Obsidian
chain.desc: Four obsidian and four sticks around a framed cube give sixteen reinforcements. Applying one makes a framed block blast-resistant while it keeps whatever texture it is wearing.

chain.title: Locking the Shape
chain.desc: Two wooden rods, a framed cube and two iron nuggets. The key locks a framed block's state so that neighbours can no longer make it change shape.

chain.title: Storage That Is Not There
chain.desc: Eight framed cubes in a ring. It stores like a chest and wears like a wall, which is the entire point.

chain.title: The Chest With No Lid
chain.desc: A framed chest plus more framed cubes. Secret storage looks exactly like the block it is camouflaged as and gives no visual clue that it opens at all.

chain.title: Seen From Only One Side
chain.desc: Four framed cubes around a block of tinted glass gives four windows. The wrench sets which single face you can see through, and crouching with the wrench clears it again.

chain.title: Light Without a Lamp
chain.desc: A framed cube and glowstone dust. Its light level is a server config value, so a pack can dim or brighten every glowing framed block at once.

chain.title: A Frame Made of Wall
chain.desc: A framed cube and leather. Hit it with the framed hammer to swap its backing between plain leather and whatever camo it is wearing, and a glow ink sac upgrades it to the glowing version.

chain.title: Pull the Face In
chain.desc: Four collapsible blocks from a ring of framed cubes. Each corner of a face can be dented independently, which is how the mod produces shapes no fixed geometry could cover.

chain.title: Slime Under the Skin
chain.desc: A framed cube and four slimeballs. It bounces like a slime block while looking like stone, wood or anything else you feed it.

chain.title: Redstone in Costume
chain.desc: A framed cube, a hay block and redstone. Every redstone component in the mod - lever, torch, buttons, pressure plates, target, redstone block - exists so a wiring run can vanish into the wall.

notes: A BUILDING-TOOL MOD WITH A REAL TIER LADDER, NOT A COSMETIC ONE - THE CHAIN IS EARNED. Verified against FramedBlocks-9.4.3.jar; META-INF/mods.toml declares modId=framedblocks, version 9.4.3, modLoader=javafml, minecraft [1.20.1,), forge [47.1.3,). The Modrinth 9.4.3 file lists loaders=[forge, neoforge] and game_versions=[1.20.1]. ID DETECTION AND WIDENING: 200 item models, 206 blockstates, 209 lang block./item. keys; models INTERSECT lang = 198, and that is the count used. WIDENING CONSIDERED AND REJECTED for the 14 blockstate-only stems - framed_wall_sign, framed_wall_hanging_sign, framed_wall_torch, framed_redstone_wall_torch, framed_soul_wall_torch, the four framed_waterloggable_*_pressure_plate entries, framed_checkered_cube_segment, framed_checkered_panel_segment, framed_checkered_slab_segment and framed_masonry_corner_segment. These are placed-state blocks and internal segments, not item forms: wall variants reuse the standing sign or torch item, the waterloggable plates are the state the framed hammer toggles a normal plate into, and the *_segment blocks are the halves a checkered or masonry block splits into in-world. NARROWED for the 2 model-only stems: framed_blueprint_written is the filled-blueprint predicate model of framedblocks:framed_blueprint, and framed_fence_inventory is the inventory model of framedblocks:framed_wall - neither is a registered id. RECIPE GRAPH: 408 recipe files across 112 distinct shapes, but the structure is far simpler than that number suggests. 173 of them are the custom type framedblocks:frame - that is the Framing Saw recipe set, one per convertible block, which is why the saw is a chain step rather than a footnote. Of the remaining crafting recipes, everything traces to framedblocks:framed_cube (four sticks and four planks, yields 4). Verified yields: framed_slab 6, framed_panel 6, framed_pane 12, framed_slope 3, framed_stairs 4, framed_bars 16, framed_reinforcement 16, framed_ladder 3, framed_door 3, framed_torch 4, framed_one_way_window 4, framed_collapsible_block 4, framed_lattice_block 3, framed_gate 4 from a framed door. THE MECHANIC THAT MAKES THE GRAPH: framedblocks:framed_hammer and framedblocks:framed_wrench appear as INGREDIENTS in dozens of shaped and shapeless recipes without being consumed. The hammer cuts a shape into a sharper one (slope to prism, slab to floor board, slope panel to flat inner slope panel corner); the wrench rotates a shape between its slab and panel spellings and between horizontal and vertical stairs, and almost every one of those conversions is reversible. That is why both tools sit at steps 2 and 3 and why the wheels below are reachable only after them. DISTINCT RECIPE SHAPES: 112 by pattern, but functionally 5 - frame-cube crafting, hammer cutting, wrench rotation, framing-saw conversion, and a handful of one-off special blocks. CONFIG GATES (server config, from lang/en_us.json): allowBlockEntities decides whether blocks with block entities can be used as camo, consumeCamoItem decides whether applying a camo eats the item, enableIntangibleFeature and intangibleMarkerItem control intangibility entirely, glowstoneLightLevel sets what framed_glowing_cube emits, oneWayWindowOwnable restricts one-way windows to their owner, and fireproofBlocks is a common-config switch. None of these removes a recipe - no recipe in this jar carries a forge:conditional wrapper - but enableIntangibleFeature set to false makes the intangibility half of framed_blueprint's payload inert. MODDB: no consensus signal - moddb.json has no framedblocks key - so the ordering is the recipe graph alone; no conflict to record. DROPS BY THE DESIRABILITY RULE (present and obtainable, deliberately unquested): framed_wall, framed_fence_gate, framed_sign, framed_hanging_sign, framed_trapdoor, framed_button and the several dozen framed_flat_*_corner and framed_*_corner_slope_panel permutations, which are wheel material at best. NOTHING WAS DROPPED AS UNOBTAINABLE - every one of the 198 verified ids is produced by at least one crafting recipe or one framedblocks:frame saw recipe.
